_classes.E1: HEADLINE-AS-MARGINALIA: spread-headline summary phrase named MN; it is running-head furniture
_classes.E2: PAGE NUMBER MISNAMED: head-band page number named MN or abstained ?? instead of PN
_classes.E3: CATCHWORD UNBOXED: Surya emits no box for the foot catchword, so it cannot be named
_classes.E4: SIGNATURE/CATCHWORD SWAP: the signature named CW (or the reverse)
_classes.E5: NOTE COLUMN SWALLOWED: marginal column inside the MT box instead of its own
_classes.E6: AR/MT VERTICAL OVERLAP: argument foot cuts into body head, clipping a line
_classes.E7: NESTED/DUPLICATE BOXES: two boxes on one object with different classes
_classes.E8: MARGIN NOTE NAMED MT: a margin note falls inside the measure and is named MainText
_classes.E9: NOTE MISSED: a visible margin note gets no box at all
_classes.E10: PARATEXT HAS NO GRAMMAR: CLASSES describes a scriptural opening; on paratext the label overflows into whichever class is nearest a containment class. SG and CH both act as containment, not only MT
_classes.E11: BLEED-THROUGH BOXED: a box on verso show-through, i.e. on ink not present on this leaf
_classes.E12: ORNAMENT GIVEN A TEXT CLASS, AND THE CLASS DRIFTS: fleurons, headpieces, tailpieces and woodcut initials have been named MT, CH, SG, MN and RH across the corpus — five classes for one non-textual object
_classes.E13: COLUMN STRUCTURE LOST: multi-column matter taken as one block. Not only tables — NT-1582-B_0438 sets a two-column parallel comparison inside the body and it is wrapped as a single MT
_classes.E14: ARGUMENT NAMED CH: argument prose named CH although AR exists in CLASSES
_classes.E15: ANNOTATIONS GENRE UNSTABLE: the annotation block is named MT, SG or CH depending on where foot_y lands. Three labels for one genre, sometimes within a single leaf
_classes.E16: TEXT OUTSIDE THE FRAME IS RENAMED: whatever falls above head_y or below foot_y changes class regardless of what it is. Body verses become SG, body continuations become CH. This is the SAME root cause as E15 and as the frame-anchor finding
_classes.E17: MARGIN NOTE NAMED CH: a margin note taken as a chapter head
_classes.E18: MN AS A FOURTH CONTAINMENT CLASS: on the harmony/synopsis pages nearly every box is named MN, including the display title and the signature. MT, SG, CH and now MN have all acted as containment
_classes.E19: SIGNATURE AND CATCHWORD MERGED INTO ONE BOX, or the signature given yet another class (CH on NT-1582-B_0777). The foot furniture has no stable treatment anywhere in the corpus
_classes.E20: CLASS DECIDED BY POSITION AGAINST THE MEASURE: identical marginal cites are named MN on one side of the measure and MT on the other. Which side gets which INVERTS between leaves (right=MT on OT1-1609-P_0010, left=MT on _0021), because the measure lands differently each time. The label tracks the frame, not the object
_classes.E21: OVERLAPPING SIBLING BOXES: adjacent boxes of the same class overlap or nest, so one line of text belongs to two regions at once
_classes.E22: GENRE IS NOT LEAF-ALIGNED: a genre with no class in CLASSES (the key to the marks) shares a leaf with ordinary matter, so the leaf cannot be excluded wholesale. Scope decisions cannot reach it
_classes.E23: EMPTY BOX: a region drawn over blank paper, carrying a class but no ink
_classes.E24: HEAD-BAND CLASS INTERCHANGE: the structural head classes swap freely. Chapter head named RH (OT2-1610-P_0865, giving two stacked RH boxes) or MN (_0666); running head named CH (_0034) or MN or MT. RH, CH and MN are not separated by any stable cue
_classes.E25: STRUCTURAL FURNITURE UNBOXED: a CHAPTER HEAD or RUNNING HEAD gets no box at all (CHAP. II. on OT1-1609-P_0348, CHAP. I. on _1015, PSALME X. on OT2-1610-P_0034; running head absent on _0276 and _0666). Distinct from E9, which covers marginal apparatus. This is the page's structural spine going missing, not its apparatus
_classes.E26: BODY BLOCK UNBOXED: the scripture column ITSELF gets no region. Not a missed note — the main text of the leaf is unclaimed (OT2-1610-P_0749, _0821, _0024, _0035 and OT1-1609-P_1011). ⚠️ CITATION CORRECTED 2026-08-29: the Osee-1011 exemplar was written as a bare ordinal under the OT2 prefix it inherited from its neighbours, and NO SUCH OT2 LEAF EXISTS. A bare leaf ordinal is not an address; it takes the witness from whatever preceded it. ⚠️ This note deliberately spells no bare ordinal of its own — the first version did, and the checker resolved it against the wrong prefix and re-reported the very defect the note describes. The most severe detection failure in the corpus
_classes.E27: SIGNATURE UNBOXED: the printed quire signature gets no box (OT1-1609-P_0661 'Hhhh 3', OT2-1610-P_0459 'I ii 2', OT2-1610-P_0902 'D'). ⚠️ CITATION CORRECTED 2026-08-29: the 'Hhhh 3' exemplar was written as a bare ordinal under the OT2 prefix; no such OT2 leaf exists and the leaf is the OT1 one named above. The twin of E3; E4/E19 cover only signatures that were MISnamed
_classes.E28: BODY TEXT NAMED CH: ordinary prose or scripture given the chapter-head class (OT2-1610-P_0820, _0035). On _0274 the assignment is INVERTED — Psalm verse text is CH and the commentary is MT
